newsitem.title: USA: Montgomery Ward rejects bid from HFS for Signature.
newsitem.headline: Montgomery Ward rejects bid from HFS for Signature.

text.p: Montgomery Ward Holding Corp., which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection last week, said Friday its board rejected a revised bid from HFS Inc. for its Signature Group direct marketing unit.

Montgomery Ward did not disclose the size of the offer but said it would not accept anything less than $1 billion for Signature. The offer from HFS was "highly conditional" and had an "impossible deadline" for closing, the company said in a statement.

"Signature is an extremely valuable business," Chairman Roger Goddu said in a statement. "The offer from HFS is wholly inadequate and unreasonable on several levels. There's no reason whatever to consider an offer that doesn't maximize the value of Signature."

The retailer had been negotiating with HFS since the spring, and the potential deal for Signature "had always involved a figure in excess of $1 billion," said Ward spokeswoman Judy Gustafson. Parsippany, N.J.,-based HFS is a large hotel franchiser and owner of Avis car rental company.

The 125-year-old retailer sought a buyer for Signature in an effort to raise cash for its ailing retail operation. The company said it has enough financial resources to complete a turnaround of its business but has not ruled out selling Signature, which has about $830 million in revenues.
"We will analyse everything that makes sense relative to our financial restructuring," Gustafson said.
